requirements.title: Opening hub's event stream in the hub client
requirements.rationale: The service needs a hub client call that opens the event stream and classifies its refusals as the other hub calls do.

criteria.condition: a caller opens the event stream for a workspace slug with a PAT
criteria.action: send `GET /api/v1/events?workspace=<query-escaped slug>` with `Authorization: Bearer <PAT>`, `Accept: text/event-stream` and the client's `User-Agent`, without following redirects
criteria.contract: on `200` with content type `text/event-stream`, an open stream reader is returned and nil error

setup: an httptest server that records the request and answers 200 text/event-stream
a hub client built with hub.New
check.pseudocode: r, err := c.Events(ctx, pat, slug); assert err==nil && r!=nil; assert srv.last.URL.RawQuery == "workspace="+url.QueryEscape(slug); assert headers

criteria.action: wait at most 10 s for the response headers, then read the body with no overall timeout until the caller's context ends
criteria.contract: a server that sends no headers for 10 s yields an `*hub.UnavailableError`; an open stream ends only when the context is cancelled or the server ends it

setup: the client's header bound shortened for the test
one server that delays its headers past the bound
one server that answers at once and then sends a frame after the bound has elapsed
check.pseudocode: _,err := Events(slow); assert errors.As(err,&ue); r := Events(fast); sleep(bound*2); srv.send(frame); assert r.Next()==frame; cancel(); assert r.Next() errors

criteria.condition: hub answers the events route with `401` or `403`
criteria.action: return a refusal; for `403` the message names the scope `audit:read` and the route `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}`
criteria.contract: `401`: `errors.Is(err, hub.ErrRefused)`; `403`: `errors.Is(err, hub.ErrForbidden)`

setup: a server answering hub's error object with 401, then with 403
check.pseudocode: assert errors.Is(e401, ErrRefused); assert errors.Is(e403, ErrForbidden); assert contains(e403.Error(), "audit:read")

criteria.condition: hub answers the events route with `404`, or with another 4xx status other than 429
criteria.action: return not found for `404`, and a rejection carrying hub's error code and message for the other 4xx statuses
criteria.contract: `404`: `errors.Is(err, hub.ErrNotFound)`; other 4xx: `*hub.RejectedError` with `Status`, `Code` and `Message` set and `errors.Is(err, hub.ErrRejected)`

setup: servers answering 404, 400, 409 and 422 with hub's {error:{code,message,error_type}} object
check.pseudocode: for s in [400,409,422]: var re *RejectedError; assert errors.As(err,&re) && re.Status==s && re.Code!="" && re.Message!=""

criteria.condition: hub answers with 429 or 5xx, the transport fails or times out, hub redirects, or a `200` carries a content type other than `text/event-stream`
criteria.action: return hub unavailable
criteria.contract: `*hub.UnavailableError` carrying the status (0 for transport failures)

setup: servers answering 429, 500, 503, a redirect, 200 text/html, and one that hangs up
check.pseudocode: for c in cases: var ue *UnavailableError; assert errors.As(err,&ue) && ue.Status==c.status

criteria.action: for any PAT and any answer of the events route, return errors and values whose text does not contain the PAT
criteria.contract: `strings.Contains(err.Error(), pat)` is false for every returned error

setup: a server whose answers may echo the Authorization header into the body or message
check.pseudocode: forall pat, status: _,err := Events(ctx, pat, slug); assert err==nil || !contains(err.Error(), pat)

requirements.title: Reading and decoding frames, and the fake hub's stream
requirements.rationale: Hub's event shape is unverified, so the client reads every plausible encoding, and only internal/hub knows hub's field names.

criteria.action: read frames by SSE rules: the fields `id:`, `event:` and `data:`, data lines joined with a line break, a line starting with a colon as a comment, and a frame with no data as no event
criteria.contract: each blank-line-terminated frame yields at most one event with the joined data

setup: a byte stream with id:, event:, multi-line data:, comment lines, a data-less frame and CRLF and LF line ends
check.pseudocode: r := newReader(bytes); events := drain(r); assert events == [{data:"a\nb"}]

criteria.action: deliver every frame and every comment to the caller as activity, including frames whose data is not a JSON object, which are activity and nothing more
criteria.contract: the caller observes one activity per frame or comment; a non-object data frame yields no decoded event

setup: a stream with two comments, a frame with JSON object data, a frame with data `hello` and a frame with data `[1,2]`
check.pseudocode: assert activities==5; assert len(events)==1

criteria.condition: a frame's data is a JSON object
criteria.action: decode a typed event: the id from JSON `id` or else the frame's `id:`, the type from JSON `event_type` or else the frame's `event:`, the workspace slug when hub names one, the issue number from `payload.issue` (integer), `payload.issue.number` or `payload.number`, and the label from `payload.label` (string) or `payload.label.name`
criteria.contract: a typed event value with ID, Type, Workspace, Issue (0 when absent) and Label (empty when absent)

setup: frames using JSON id/event_type, frame id:/event: only, payload.issue integer, payload.issue.number, payload.number, payload.label string and payload.label.name
check.pseudocode: table-driven: assert decode(frame) == Event{ID,Type,Workspace,Issue,Label}

criteria.condition: a line of the stream is longer than 1 MiB
criteria.action: end the read with an error
criteria.contract: the reader returns a non-nil error and delivers no further frames

setup: a stream with one frame, then a line of 1 MiB + 1 bytes, then another frame
check.pseudocode: assert err != nil; assert len(events)==1

criteria.action: keep hub's field names (`event_type`, `workspace_slug` and the others) inside `internal/hub`, so that no non-test Go file outside it contains them
criteria.contract: the existing field-name walk in `internal/hub/calls_test.go` passes

setup: the new stream code is in the repository
check.pseudocode: go test ./internal/hub -run FieldNames

criteria.condition: a client opens `GET /api/v1/events?workspace=<slug>` on the fake hub
criteria.action: check the token's access to the workspace as its other routes do, apply faults set through `Inject`, `Fail` and `Hangup` on that path, and otherwise hold the connection open as `text/event-stream`
criteria.contract: an unknown token gets `401`, a token without access gets hub's error status, an injected fault is served as injected, and otherwise `200` `text/event-stream`

setup: a fake hub workspace widgets with a valid token and a token with no access
check.pseudocode: assert status(unknown)==401; h.Fail("GET","/api/v1/events",503); assert status==503; assert ct=="text/event-stream"

criteria.action: let a test send an event to a workspace's open connections, send a heartbeat, end every connection of a workspace, read how many connections are open, and turn on emitting `hub.forge.issue.labeled` whenever a label is added through its forge API
criteria.contract: exported fakehub methods for each seam; a label added through the forge API with emission on reaches every open connection of the workspace as one labeled event

setup: two open events connections for widgets and one for another workspace
emission on label add is turned on
check.pseudocode: h.SendEvent(ws, ev); h.Heartbeat(ws); assert h.EventConns(ws)==2; api.AddLabel(...); assert recv.type==labeled; h.EndEvents(ws); assert h.EventConns(ws)==0

requirements.title: One stream per poll loop
requirements.rationale: The stream shares the poll's scan, state and records, so its lifecycle follows the poll loop's.

criteria.condition: the poll supervisor starts a loop for a workspace, at the first scan or at a scan that finds a new subscription
criteria.action: start one event stream for that workspace together with the loop
criteria.contract: the fake hub counts one open events connection for the workspace within one scan period (60 s on the fake clock)

setup: the poll env with a fake hub, fake clock and real store and jobs
workspace widgets subscribed after the supervisor started
check.pseudocode: env.Subscribe(); clock.Advance(60s); eventually(h.EventConns(ws)==1)

criteria.condition: a workspace's poll loop is taken away (unsubscribe, a scan that finds the subscription gone, a cycle that finds it not subscribed) or the poll stops
criteria.action: stop that workspace's event stream
criteria.contract: the fake hub counts zero open events connections for the workspace after the next scan

setup: widgets has an open events connection
check.pseudocode: store.Unsubscribe(ws); clock.Advance(60s); eventually(h.EventConns(ws)==0)

criteria.condition: the stream opens a connection
criteria.action: read the subscription's token from the store, then the workspace's resolved variables from hub, then the workspace record from hub for the forge repository, then connect at once with no random delay; the request labels are read from the subscription's `label_prefix` each time an event is handled
criteria.contract: the fake hub records the variable read, the record read and the events request in that order

setup: a subscribed widgets workspace and a recording fake hub
check.pseudocode: assert h.Requests()[0:3] == [vars, record, events]; assert clock.Pending()==0

criteria.condition: a scan finds that the subscription's `UpdatedAt` has changed since the stream connected
criteria.action: close the open connection and reconnect at once with the new token
criteria.contract: the next events request carries `Authorization: Bearer <new PAT>`

setup: widgets connected with pat-OLD
check.pseudocode: store.Subscribe(ws, pat-NEW); clock.Advance(60s); assert lastEventsReq.Auth == "Bearer pat-NEW"; assert h.EventConns(ws)==1

criteria.condition: the store answers "not subscribed" to the stream
criteria.action: stop the stream and take the workspace's poll loop away with it, so that a later scan finding the workspace subscribed again starts both
criteria.contract: no loop and no stream remain for the workspace; after resubscribe, the next scan has one of each

setup: widgets with a loop and a stream
the store answers ErrNotSubscribed to the stream's token read
check.pseudocode: assert !sup.HasLoop(ws) && h.EventConns(ws)==0; resubscribe; clock.Advance(60s); assert sup.HasLoop(ws) && h.EventConns(ws)==1

criteria.condition: the subscription's token cannot be read (`store.ErrUnreadable`)
criteria.action: log one `ERROR` naming the token read and keep retrying at the backoff
criteria.contract: exactly one `ERROR` record across repeated attempts; connection attempts continue

setup: the subscription's token row is unreadable (store.ErrUnreadable)
check.pseudocode: assert count(logs, ERROR, "token")==1; assert attempts>=4

criteria.action: handle the events of one workspace one at a time in arrival order, and never let streams of different workspaces wait on each other
criteria.contract: a blocked event handler on one workspace does not delay the handling of an event on another workspace

setup: two subscribed workspaces
the issue read of workspace one blocks on a gate
check.pseudocode: gate.Block(ws1); send(ws1,e1); send(ws1,e2); send(ws2,e3); eventually(job(ws2)); assert !handled(e2); gate.Open(); assert order==[e1,e2]

criteria.condition: the poll supervisor stops
criteria.action: cancel every stream and any event being handled, and return only after they have returned, so that `serve` stops them before the jobs layer and before the state file is closed
criteria.contract: `Supervisor.Stop` returns with zero stream goroutines running and zero open events connections

setup: two workspaces with open streams and one event handler blocked in a hub call
check.pseudocode: sup.Stop(); assert goroutines(stream)==0; assert h.EventConns(any)==0

requirements.title: The poll's switch and reconnecting
requirements.rationale: AF_POLL_INTERVAL=0 keeps its documented meaning of turning off every label trigger, and a lost connection is recovered without hammering hub.

criteria.condition: the workspace's `AF_POLL_INTERVAL` reads as a zero duration
criteria.action: open no connection to the events route and read the variables again 5 minutes later
criteria.contract: the fake hub records no events request; a label added to an issue makes no job

setup: widgets with AF_POLL_INTERVAL set to 0 and issue 42 carrying af:fix
check.pseudocode: assert h.EventsRequests()==0; assert len(jobs)==0; h.SetVar("AF_POLL_INTERVAL","5m"); clock.Advance(5m); assert h.EventConns(ws)==1

criteria.condition: `AF_POLL_INTERVAL` changes from `0` to `5m`
criteria.action: connect at its next reading of the variables
criteria.contract: an events connection is open within 5 minutes on the fake clock

criteria.condition: a request event or closed event arrives on an open connection and the stream's reading of the variables is older than 5 minutes
criteria.action: read the variables again before acting; if the new reading is `0`, not act on the event, not record it, close the connection, and read the variables again 5 minutes later
criteria.contract: with the new reading `0`: no job, no label removal, no `af_hub_events` row, and zero open connections

setup: a connected stream whose variable reading is older than 5 minutes
the variable is now 0 and issue 42 carries af:fix
check.pseudocode: clock.Advance(6m); h.SetVar(...,"0"); h.SendEvent(labeled); assert jobs==0 && removals==0 && rows==0 && h.EventConns(ws)==0

criteria.action: stay on when `AF_POLL_INTERVAL` is unset, invalid, or a duration from 1m to 24h, and log nothing about its value
criteria.contract: no log record from the stream mentions `AF_POLL_INTERVAL`

setup: AF_POLL_INTERVAL unset, then "bogus", then "1m", then "24h"
check.pseudocode: for v in values: assert h.EventConns(ws)==1; assert !anyLog("AF_POLL_INTERVAL", fromStream)

criteria.condition: a connection fails or ends
criteria.action: wait on the poll's clock before retrying, starting at 1 s and doubling after each further failure up to 60 s, with no jitter, and without trying to recover missed events or bringing the poll's next cycle forward
criteria.contract: consecutive failing attempts wait 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60 and 60 s on the fake clock; a server-ended stream reconnects after 1 s

setup: the fake clock and a fake hub that ends the stream once, then fails every connect with 503
check.pseudocode: h.EndEvents(ws); advance(1s); assert attempts==2; h.Fail(...503); for w in [1,2,4,8,16,32,60,60]: advance(w-1); assert same; advance(1); assert attempts+1

criteria.condition: hub has been found not to serve the event stream (`404` or `405` on the events route after the workspace record was read)
criteria.action: wait 60 s before every further attempt
criteria.contract: each later attempt follows the previous one by 60 s on the fake clock

setup: the fake hub answers 404 on the events route after serving the workspace record
check.pseudocode: h.Fail(GET,events,404); assert gaps==[60s,60s,60s]

criteria.condition: a connection receives its first frame or comment
criteria.action: reset the next backoff wait to 1 s
criteria.contract: the next reconnect after that connection ends happens after 1 s

setup: several failed connects have raised the backoff to 8 s
then a connection succeeds
check.pseudocode: h.Heartbeat(ws); h.EndEvents(ws); advance(1s); assert attempts+1

criteria.condition: an open connection receives no bytes for 60 s, not counting time spent acting on an event
criteria.action: close the connection, treat it as ended, and open a new one after the backoff wait
criteria.contract: the fake hub sees the connection closed after 60 s of silence and a new events request follows

setup: an open connection that receives nothing
a second connection whose event handler is blocked for 120 s on the fake clock
check.pseudocode: advance(60s); assert h.EventConns==0; advance(1s); assert h.EventsRequests==2

requirements.title: What the stream logs
requirements.rationale: Each failure must be visible once and each recovery visible, without one kind of record silencing another.

criteria.condition: a connection receives its first frame or comment after connection failures or an outage were logged
criteria.action: log one `INFO` that the stream has recovered and reset the connection-failure records, so that a later failure is logged again
criteria.contract: one `INFO` record; the next connection failure produces a new record

setup: the events route failed with 503 and a WARN was logged
check.pseudocode: assert count(INFO,"recovered")==1; assert count(WARN,"unavailable")==2

criteria.condition: the token read, the variable read, the workspace-record read or the connect fails
criteria.action: log the failure once per kind and operation until the next activity: `ERROR` for a refused or forbidden token, a workspace hub does not find at the record read, a rejected request or an unreadable token, naming the operation and the `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` route or the scope `audit:read`, whichever cures it; `WARN` for hub unavailable; and keep retrying
criteria.contract: `401` on connect: one `ERROR` naming `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}`; `403`: one `ERROR` naming `audit:read`; `503`: one `WARN`; retries continue in each case

setup: the fake hub answers the events route with 401, then 403, then 503 in separate runs
check.pseudocode: assert one(ERROR, contains "PUT /api/v1/workspaces"); assert attempts>3

criteria.condition: the events route answers `404` or `405` after the workspace record was read
criteria.action: log one `WARN` saying that hub does not serve the event stream and that labels are found by the poll alone
criteria.contract: exactly one such `WARN` across repeated attempts

setup: the workspace record was read and the events route answers 404
check.pseudocode: assert count(WARN,"does not serve")==1; assert count(ERROR)==0

criteria.condition: the stream has had no connection with activity for longer than the poll interval it last read (5 minutes when none was read), and the `WARN` that hub does not serve the stream does not stand
criteria.action: log one `WARN` that labels are being found by the poll alone
criteria.contract: one outage `WARN` per outage; none after the not-served `WARN`

setup: AF_POLL_INTERVAL=10m read by the stream
hub answers 503 on the events route; in a second run it answers 404
check.pseudocode: advance(10m+1s); assert count(WARN,"poll alone")==1

criteria.condition: a hub call or a jobs-layer call fails while a request or closed event is handled
criteria.action: log the failure once per kind and operation until an event of the workspace is next handled without failure, classified as connection failures are, in records kept apart from the connection-failure records and the poll's failure records
criteria.contract: two request events in a row whose issue read answers `503` give one `WARN`; after an event handled without failure the next such failure is logged again; connection-failure logging is unaffected

setup: the issue read answers 503 for requests of two events in a row
connection failures are also being logged
check.pseudocode: assert count(WARN,"issue read")==1 after e1,e2; h.clear(); e3 ok; h.Fail(503); e4; assert count==2

criteria.condition: a malformed event arrives
criteria.action: ignore it with no request to hub and log it at `WARN` once per connection
criteria.contract: one `WARN` per connection however many malformed events arrive on it

setup: a connection receiving labeled events with a request label and no id, no issue number, a 257-byte id and an id with a control character, plus a closed event with no issue
then a reconnect
check.pseudocode: assert h.ForgeRequests()==0; assert count(WARN,"malformed")==1; reconnect; send(bad); assert ==2

criteria.action: log every other ignored event, including an event of another type without an issue number, at `DEBUG` at most
criteria.contract: no record above `DEBUG` for ignored events that are not malformed

setup: a connection with DEBUG logging captured
check.pseudocode: assert maxLevel(logs)<=DEBUG

criteria.action: for any failure and any event, write log records that do not contain the subscription's PAT
criteria.contract: no captured log line contains the PAT

setup: a subscription with a random PAT and a hub that may echo the token into error bodies
check.pseudocode: forall pat, failure, event: run(); assert !contains(logBuffer.String(), pat)

requirements.title: A labeled event goes through the poll's rules
requirements.rationale: The stream must run the same rules as a cycle, or it would take back labels the worker restored or make a second job for a label whose removal is owed.

criteria.action: treat as a request only a request event, hand closed events to the closed handling, and ignore every other event (another label, another type, another workspace, malformed) with no request to hub
criteria.contract: labeled events for `af:ready` or `bug`, and events of other types, produce no recorded request on the fake hub

setup: a connected stream for widgets with prefix af:
check.pseudocode: assert len(h.ForgeRequests())==0

criteria.condition: a request event arrives
criteria.action: under the per-workspace lock, ignore the event if its id is recorded, make sure the poll is on, read the issue through hub's forge API, and do nothing more if the issue is closed, is a pull request, or no longer carries the label (case ignored)
criteria.contract: a repeated event id sends no forge request; a closed, pull-request or unlabelled issue gets no job and no label removal

setup: issues: 50 closed with af:fix, 51 a pull request with af:fix, 52 open without af:fix, 53 open with af:fix already handled by evt-9
check.pseudocode: assert jobs==0; assert requestsAfterRepeat == requestsBefore

criteria.condition: a request event arrives for an issue that hub reads as open and carrying the label and no open job of that kind absorbs it, no hold holds it and no removal is owed
criteria.action: create a job with `source` `{"kind": "event", "by": "<event id>"}`, `request_label` the canonical label and the issue number as input, write the poll record, then remove the label through hub
criteria.contract: within 1 s: one job with `input` `{"issue": 42}`, one poll record, one `DELETE` of the label on the fake hub, in that order of record then removal

setup: issue 42 open with af:fix and no job
check.pseudocode: h.SetRemovalLag(42); send(evt1); eventually(len(jobs)==1, 1s); assert doc.source=={"event","evt-1"}; send(evt1); sup.Cycle(); assert len(jobs)==1

criteria.condition: a request event arrives for an open issue carrying the label and an open job of that kind exists for the issue, or the jobs layer refuses the create as a duplicate
criteria.action: absorb the label: remove it, or record the removal as owed if the removal fails, and make no job
criteria.contract: no new job; one label removal sent, or an owed poll record

setup: issue 60 with an open fix job made through the API
issue 61 likewise, whose label removal fails with 422
check.pseudocode: assert len(jobs(60))==1; assert removals(60)==1; assert rec(61).Owed

criteria.condition: a request event arrives for an open issue carrying the label and a poll record holds that label (a restore by the worker or cleanup)
criteria.action: do nothing to the issue and record the event as decided
criteria.contract: no job, no label removal; the label stays on the issue

setup: a stream-made job cancelled while in a runner, with the worker putting af:fix back and a hold in the poll record
check.pseudocode: assert jobs==1(cancelled); assert removals==0; assert rowExists(evt)

criteria.condition: a request event arrives for an open issue carrying the label and the label's removal is owed by an earlier request
criteria.action: remove the label again and make no job
criteria.contract: no new job; one label removal sent

setup: a stream-made job whose label removal failed with 422 so the removal is owed
check.pseudocode: assert removals==2; assert len(jobs)==1; assert !rec.Owed or dropped

criteria.condition: the jobs layer refuses the create with "not subscribed" or with any refusal other than a duplicate
criteria.action: for "not subscribed", end the handling with no label written; for any other refusal, log an event-handling failure at `WARN` and leave the label
criteria.contract: no job, no label removal, no recorded event id

setup: a jobs layer that refuses Create with ErrNotSubscribed, and another that refuses with an internal error
check.pseudocode: assert removals==0 && rows==0; assert count(WARN)==1 for other

criteria.condition: hub cannot be asked, or refuses the variable read, the issue read or the label removal, while a request event is handled
criteria.action: leave the event to the poll: the label stays or its removal stays owed, the event id is not recorded, and the failure is logged as an event-handling failure
criteria.contract: no `af_hub_events` row for the event; a later poll cycle can still take the label

setup: the variable read, the issue read or the label removal fails in separate runs (503 and 401)
check.pseudocode: assert rows==0; sup.Cycle(); assert len(jobs)==1

requirements.title: Event ids and the poll's side of sharing the rules
requirements.rationale: A stream event and a poll cycle must never make two jobs for one request, and delivered events must not be acted on twice.

criteria.condition: a request event or closed event is decided (job made, label absorbed or removed again, hold left alone, cancel made, or nothing to do because of hub's read of the issue)
criteria.action: record its id in `af_hub_events`, keyed by workspace and event id, with the time it was taken, through one migration appended after `agent_fox_label_protocol`'s
criteria.contract: one `af_hub_events` row per decided event; the same id sent again makes no job and sends no forge request

setup: a request event that makes a job and a closed event that cancels one
check.pseudocode: assert count(rows)==2; assert h.ForgeRequests()==before

criteria.condition: an event is ignored, is a closed event for an issue with no open job, is not acted on because the poll is off, or its handling failed
criteria.action: not record its id
criteria.contract: no `af_hub_events` row for the event

setup: an ignored event, a closed event for an issue with no open job, a request event while the poll is off and a request event whose issue read fails
check.pseudocode: assert count(af_hub_events)==0

criteria.action: not act again on an event whose id is recorded for its workspace, across a restart of the service and independently of the jobs
criteria.contract: after reopening the state file, a recorded id is still ignored

setup: evt-1 recorded and the service state file closed and reopened with a new supervisor
check.pseudocode: reopen(); send(evt1); assert forgeRequests==0

criteria.condition: the poll supervisor scans the subscriptions
criteria.action: delete the event ids taken more than 7 days ago by its clock
criteria.contract: an id taken 7 days and 1 minute ago is deleted; a newer one is kept

setup: two af_hub_events rows taken 7d1m ago and 6d23h ago by the fake clock
check.pseudocode: clock.Advance(60s); assert !exists(old) && exists(new)

criteria.action: take the same per-workspace lock as the stream for one issue's rules at a time, never for a whole cycle, so that the rules of the two triggers never run at once for one workspace
criteria.contract: a stream event for a workspace is handled between two issues of a running cycle of that workspace

setup: a cycle listing two issues, whose handling of the first is paused
check.pseudocode: pause(issue1); send(evt); release(); assert order==[issue1, evt, issue2]

criteria.condition: a cycle reaches an issue whose label no open job absorbs, no hold holds and no removal is owed and a poll record of that label on that issue was made at or after the listing was requested
criteria.action: make no job and leave the label to its next cycle
criteria.contract: no create call; the label stays

setup: a listing requested at T, then a stream-made job for the same issue and label whose record was made after T and has ended
check.pseudocode: assert createCalls==0; assert labelOn(issue)

criteria.condition: a complete listing settles owed removals and releases holds and a poll record was made at or after the listing was requested
criteria.action: neither settle that record's owed removal nor release its hold
criteria.contract: the record keeps `Owed` and its hold after the cycle

setup: an owed record and a held record made at or after the listing was requested, and older ones for comparison
check.pseudocode: assert rec(new).Owed && rec(new).Hold; assert !rec(old).Owed

criteria.action: for any interleaving of a stream event and a poll cycle that see the same new request label at the same moment, end with exactly one job and the label removed, including when the forge listing still shows the label after removal (removal lag)
criteria.contract: over 50 rounds, each round has one job and the label is off the issue

setup: fresh issue per round, removal lag set so the listing may still show the label
check.pseudocode: for i in 1..50: add(issue_i, af:fix); go send(evt_i); go cycle(); wait(); assert len(jobs(i))==1 && !hasLabel(i)

requirements.title: A closed event cancels the issue's open jobs
requirements.rationale: An issue that is closed has no use for any job about it, and a cancel throws work away, so it acts on hub's current view.

criteria.condition: a closed event arrives
criteria.action: under the per-workspace lock, ignore it if its id is recorded, then look in the job records for the workspace's open jobs (queued, running or blocked, triage or fix, any source) of that issue, and with none stop with nothing recorded
criteria.contract: with no open job: no request to hub, no `af_hub_events` row, no log record above `DEBUG`

setup: issue 70 with no open job, and DEBUG-and-above logging captured
check.pseudocode: assert h.Requests()==baseline; assert rows==0; assert maxLevel<=DEBUG

criteria.condition: a closed event arrives and the issue has at least one open job
criteria.action: make sure the poll is on, read the issue through hub, and cancel nothing when hub reads it as open
criteria.contract: an issue read as open leaves every job in its state

setup: issue 71 with a queued fix job and a running triage job, and hub reading the issue as open
check.pseudocode: assert states==[queued,running]

criteria.condition: a closed event arrives for an issue with open jobs and hub reads the issue as closed
criteria.action: cancel every open job of the issue, as found at that moment, with the issue-closed cause, and log one `INFO` naming the workspace, the issue and the cancelled job ids
criteria.contract: each job reads `state` `cancelled` with `cancel_cause` `"issue_closed"`; one `INFO` record

setup: issue 72 with a queued fix job and a blocked triage job, and hub reading it as closed
check.pseudocode: for j in jobs: assert j.state=="cancelled" && j.cancel_cause=="issue_closed"; assert one(INFO, ws, 72, ids)

criteria.condition: hub cannot read the issue for a closed event
criteria.action: cancel nothing, not record the event, and log an event-handling failure
criteria.contract: jobs keep their state; no `af_hub_events` row; one log record per kind and operation

setup: issue 73 with an open job and the issue read answering 503
check.pseudocode: assert state==running; assert rows==0; assert count(WARN,"issue read")==1

criteria.action: run an issue-closed cancel as the ordinary cancel except for its recorded cause and its labels: cancel queued attempts, tell a running attempt's runner with `jobs.ErrIssueClosed` (wrapping `ErrCancelled`) and give it the 60 s grace, emit `job_state`, and treat the cause as a cancel at lease release, grace and recovery
criteria.contract: `errors.Is(cause, jobs.ErrCancelled)` and `errors.Is(cause, jobs.ErrIssueClosed)` both hold for the runner's cause; a `job_state` event is emitted

setup: the jobs layer with fakerunner blocking a running attempt
check.pseudocode: c := runner.Call.Cause(); assert Is(c,ErrCancelled) && Is(c,ErrIssueClosed); assert events has job_state

criteria.condition: a job changes state between the look and the cancel
criteria.action: look at the job again and retry the cancel, at most 8 times, as the unsubscribe's cancel does
criteria.contract: the job ends `cancelled` with `cancel_cause` `"issue_closed"`, or the retry gives up after 8 tries with an error returned to the stream

setup: a job that moves from queued to running between the look and the cancel, and one that changes state on every try
check.pseudocode: assert doc.cancel_cause=="issue_closed"; assert tries==8 && err!=nil

criteria.action: store the cause of every cancel with the job, in the same migration as `af_hub_events`, and show it in the job document as `cancel_cause`
criteria.contract: `"cancelled"` for a person's cancel, `"unsubscribed"` for an unsubscribe, `"issue_closed"` for an issue-closed cancel, `null` for a job not cancelled or cancelled before this release

setup: jobs cancelled by a person, by an unsubscribe and by an issue close, a running job and a job cancelled before the migration (null column)
check.pseudocode: assert docs.map(cancel_cause)==["cancelled","unsubscribed","issue_closed",nil,nil]

criteria.condition: the jobs layer writes the envelope for an issue-closed attempt whose runner returned without one or overran the grace
criteria.action: write the envelope with category `cancelled` and a message saying that the issue was closed
criteria.contract: envelope `error.category` `cancelled`; `error.message` mentions that the issue was closed

setup: a runner that returns without an envelope, and one that overruns the 60 s grace, both cancelled with the issue-closed cause
check.pseudocode: assert env.error.category=="cancelled"; assert contains(lower(env.error.message),"closed")

requirements.title: An issue-closed cancel removes its jobs' status labels and adds none
requirements.rationale: Labels mirror the job record, so a closed issue keeps no status label of a cancelled job, and nothing is put back on it.

criteria.condition: an issue-closed cancel reaches a runner that has opened its hub session
criteria.action: release the lease, report to hub, return within the grace, and on the issue only take off the `af:in-progress` it set; an attempt stopped before its loop ended writes an envelope with category `cancelled` and a message saying the issue was closed
criteria.contract: the lease is released; `af:in-progress` is removed; no label added and no comment posted on the fake hub

setup: a running fix job made by the stream with its hub session open and af:in-progress set on issue 42
check.pseudocode: assert doc.attempt.state=="cancelled"; assert leaseReleased; assert !has(42,"af:in-progress"); assert adds==0 && comments==0

criteria.condition: an issue-closed cancel reaches no runner, or a runner without a hub session
criteria.action: run `agent_fox_label_protocol`'s cancel cleanup with its marks, tries, retries and give-up, making only its step-3 removals (`af:in-progress` unless another job of the issue is running, and the labels in the job's `labels.set` unless another open job of the issue shows them) and never its step-4 restore
criteria.contract: `labels.cleanup` reads `"pending"` then `"done"`, or `"label_not_set"` where that spec's R5 says so; `af:needs-human` of a blocked job and a left `af:in-progress` are removed

setup: issue 43 with a blocked triage job showing af:needs-human set, carrying af:landed
issue 44 with a fix job whose attempt was shut down and left af:in-progress
check.pseudocode: assert history(cleanup)==[pending,done]; assert labels(43)==[af:landed]; assert !has(44,in-progress)

criteria.action: keep `labels.restore` `null` for every issue-closed cancel and add nothing to the issue: no request label, no status label, no comment
criteria.contract: the fake hub records no label addition and no comment for the issue after the cancel

setup: issue-closed cancels of a running job, a blocked job and a queued job, with the fake hub recording every write
check.pseudocode: assert doc.labels.restore==nil; assert h.Writes(kind in [addLabel,comment])==0

criteria.action: leave on the issue every label the cancelled jobs do not account for, such as a person's label or `af:landed` of an earlier job
criteria.contract: `af:landed` stays on issue 43 after the cleanup

criteria.condition: the jobs layer is built without a forge
criteria.action: write nothing to the issue for an issue-closed cancel
criteria.contract: no forge request is sent for the cancel

setup: a jobs layer built with no forge and an open job
check.pseudocode: assert h.ForgeRequests()==0

criteria.action: read the cancel cause through `jobs.Standing` and have `note` treat a job cancelled with `issue_closed` as ended and holding nothing, whether or not the cancel reached a runner and whatever its cleanup shows
criteria.contract: the poll record of such a job reads `seen` `ended` with no hold

setup: poll records for jobs cancelled with issue_closed, one whose cancel reached a runner (cancelled in runner) and one whose cleanup is pending or failed
check.pseudocode: assert rec.Seen=="ended" && !rec.Held

criteria.condition: an issue whose jobs were cancelled with `issue_closed` is reopened and labelled `af:fix`
criteria.action: make a new job for the next request event, and let the next poll cycle make one when no event is sent
criteria.contract: one new fix job per trigger; the label is removed

setup: issue 42 whose jobs were cancelled with issue_closed, then reopened and labelled af:fix
check.pseudocode: send(evt); assert newJobs==1; (second) sup.Cycle(); assert newJobs==1

execution_paths.title: A person's request label becomes a job through the event stream

steps.action: adds `af:fix` to open issue 42 of workspace `widgets`
sends a `hub.forge.issue.labeled` frame with id `evt-1`, issue 42 and label `af:fix` on the workspace's events connection
decodes the event, takes the per-workspace lock, finds `evt-1` unrecorded and the poll on, and reads issue 42 through hub as open and carrying `af:fix`
creates a fix job with `source` `{"kind": "event", "by": "evt-1"}`, `request_label` `af:fix` and `input` `{"issue": 42}`
inserts the owed poll record for the job and the `af_hub_events` row for `evt-1`
receives one `DELETE` of `af:fix` from issue 42, and the job exists within one second of the event

setup: fake hub with workspace widgets subscribed with prefix af:, open issue 42 carrying af:fix, real store and jobs layer on a temp state file, fakerunner and fakeclock
end_state: within 1 s one fix job exists with source {kind:event,by:evt-1}, request_label af:fix, input {issue:42}
one poll record is written and one af_hub_events row for evt-1
one DELETE of af:fix from issue 42 reaches the fake hub

execution_paths.title: Closing an issue stops its running job

steps.action: closes issue 42, whose fix job is running and has set `af:in-progress`
sends a `hub.forge.issue.closed` event for issue 42
finds the open job in the job records, confirms the poll is on, and reads issue 42 through hub as closed
cancels the job with the issue-closed cause, stores `cancel_cause` `issue_closed` with `labels.restore` `null`, emits `job_state` and tells the runner with the 60 s grace
releases its lease, reports to hub, takes `af:in-progress` off issue 42 and writes a `cancelled` envelope saying the issue was closed
records the event id and logs one `INFO` naming `widgets`, issue 42 and the cancelled job

setup: fake hub, real store and jobs layer, real worker runner with hub session, issue 42 with a running stream-made fix job that set af:in-progress
end_state: the job reads cancelled with cancel_cause issue_closed and labels.restore null
the lease is released and af:in-progress is removed
no label added, no comment posted
one INFO names widgets, 42 and the job id and the event id is recorded

execution_paths.title: Closing an issue with a blocked job cleans up its status label

steps.action: closes issue 43, whose triage job is blocked with `af:needs-human` set and which also carries `af:landed`
sends a `hub.forge.issue.closed` event for issue 43
finds the blocked job, reads issue 43 as closed, and asks the jobs layer to cancel the issue's open jobs
cancels the job with `cancel_cause` `issue_closed`, marks `labels.cleanup` `pending`, removes `af:needs-human` without adding any label, and sets `labels.cleanup` `done`
notes the job as ended and holding nothing, so issue 43 keeps `af:landed` and a later `af:fix` on the reopened issue makes a new job

end_state: the job reads cancelled with cancel_cause issue_closed, labels.cleanup pending then done, labels.restore null

the poll notes the job ended with no hold and the cycle makes one new fix job
